_: The two hand-kept halves of one rule: nothing in Steward is German.
The list of German words is NOT here. It is derived, by both tests that enforce this rule,
bilingual bundle this project maintains anyway, which is 601 words of real German and grows
on its own. What is here is only what a derivation cannot know.
Read by steward-ui/frontend/src/language.test.ts and by NothingIsGermanTest. One file, because
two copies of a rule is one copy that is quietly out of date.
_alsoEnglish: Words that are in the German bundle and are also English words. Every one was checked by
hand against the sources here. This list is expected to grow by one whenever an English
sentence trips it - the test goes red once, somebody reads the word, and adds it. That is the
right failure: loud, and one line to answer. A guard that reports a false positive and is
then deleted is the failure this shape avoids.
_extra: German words that the bundle does not contain and that were found in Steward anyway. This is
the memory of what actually leaked - it is not a dictionary and must not become one.
_stems: MEASURED 2026-09-14, and this is why the derivation is not enough on its own: the bundle says
`Befehl` and Steward said `Befehle`; the bundle says `Konfigurationsdateien` and Steward said
`Konfiguration`. Both guards matched whole words, so both walked past. A derived list knows
the forms the bot happens to use, and German inflects and compounds.
So a word in a source file is German in two more cases. INFLECTION: it is a derived word of
`minStem` letters plus one of `tails` - German endings only, which is why `stopped` does not
count as `stoppe` plus a `d`. COMPOUNDING: it is at least `minPrefix` letters and a derived
word continues it by at least `minRest` - `argument` inside `argumente` is one letter and is
not a compound, `Konfiguration` inside `Konfigurationsdateien` is eight and is.
MEASURED with these numbers on 2026-09-14: zero false positives across the whole frontend and
all three Java trees. A false positive is one line in alsoEnglish, which is the failure this
whole file is shaped around - but the numbers are chosen so it stays rare.
_shapes: The second check, and it is beside the derivation rather than part of it: these find German
by its SHAPE, so they work on words the bot has never said. `Gelaufen` was one - it is in no
bundle, no stem of it is, and it was on the run list of the operations page.
WHAT THESE DO NOT FIND, written down because a guard that hides its blind spot is worse than
one that has none: a word with no German ending. `Sperre` and `streiten` both leaked on
2026-09-14 and neither has a shape - they are a hand-list job, which is what `extra` is.
`ge...t` participles (`gemacht`, `gesagt`) are deliberately NOT here: `government` and
`gentlest` are the same shape, and a guard that cries on `government` gets deleted.
The third pattern was added the same day for `Verwerfen`, which sat on the config form's
discard button and was in no bundle, no stem and neither of the first two shapes. MEASURED
across the frontend and all three Java trees: zero lines match it that are not German.
